macro_summary: Markets enter September 4 facing back-to-back macro binaries: the August NFP print due at 8:30 AM ET today and an FOMC rate decision on September 16 where hike/hold odds sit near 50/50. The Nasdaq rallied 1.4% Thursday and VIX fell to ~14-15, reflecting low complacency ahead of significant event risk. Tech continues to dominate S&P 500 earnings contribution, supported by the ongoing AI capex supercycle, while geopolitical risk (Iran, trade) remains a tail concern for semiconductor names.

ideas.name: SK Hynix Inc. Sponsored ADR
ideas.thesis: SKHY appeared in all 6 overnight screens — the strongest consensus of the session. The ADR offers the cheapest large-cap entry into HBM/AI memory at a TTM P/E of ~6.23x, a deep discount to semiconductor peers, with a $28.6B share buyback program (backed by $49.7B net cash) providing a hard technical floor near current levels. Direct structural lock-in to Nvidia's $500B+ AI infrastructure roadmap and a $4B Indiana HBM fab investment (announced Aug 27) reinforce the secular growth runway.
ideas.catalyst: Bernstein Buy rating initiated Sep 1, 2026; $4B Indiana HBM production hub MOU with Purdue announced Aug 27, 2026; next earnings expected ~late Oct 2026; $28.6B buyback ongoing
ideas.edge: TTM P/E of 6.23x vs. semiconductor peer average; stock at ~$164 vs. July 14 high of $194.80 (~15% below recent peak); $28.6B active buyback vs. $49.7B net cash creates a quantifiable price floor; IPO priced Jul 10 at $149
ideas.bull_case: Buyback mechanics + Nvidia supply-chain lock-in drive a re-rating toward peer multiples; Bernstein Buy and Indiana fab announcement bring institutional attention to an under-followed recent IPO at an attractive entry ~15% below peak.
ideas.bear_case: Geopolitical risk (Iran, U.S.-Korea trade tensions) could trigger tech risk-off; options liquidity is limited as a recent IPO; memory cycle downturns can compress even cheap multiples further.

ideas.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ideas.thesis: NVDA appeared in all 6 overnight screens with a preference for options over outright stock. Despite a blowout fiscal Q2 FY2027 print (revenue +106% YoY to $96.2B, EPS +128%), the stock sold off ~4.6% post-earnings and sits ~43% below the consensus 12-month analyst price target of $325.99 from ~$228 current. September seasonal weakness and the Sep 16 FOMC binary make defined-risk call spreads (Oct/Nov expiry) the preferred structure, with the Nov 17 confirmed earnings date as the key re-rating catalyst.
ideas.catalyst: Post-Q2 FY27 beat sell-the-news dip ongoing; FOMC decision Sep 16, 2026 (macro binary); next earnings confirmed Nov 17, 2026 AMC
ideas.edge: Consensus analyst target $325.99 = ~43% upside from ~$228; 60 analysts rated Strong Buy; 58% projected revenue CAGR FY26-FY29; $1T order book for 2026-2027; stock trading at ~25x forward vs. Nasdaq-100 at 26x despite vastly superior growth
ideas.bull_case: AI infrastructure demand remains insatiable — a clean FOMC hold on Sep 16 removes the rate overhang and sets up a re-rating into the Nov 17 earnings print, where another beat could close the gap to consensus targets.
ideas.bear_case: September is historically weak for NVDA; a Sep 16 rate hike could spike rates and compress growth multiples; geopolitical restrictions on chip exports remain an ongoing tail risk.

ideas.name: Microsoft Corporation
ideas.thesis: MSFT appeared in 4 of 6 overnight screens, with runs consistently flagging the Oct 28, 2026 earnings date as a clean 8-week swing window. Azure is guided to accelerate to 45% growth in Q1 FY27 (per BofA note Sep 1), crossing $100B annualized, and MSFT is a direct beneficiary of $600B+ in 2026 hyperscaler AI capex. Stock trades at ~$512 vs. a BofA target of $600 and consensus target of $571. All runs preferred a defined-risk call debit spread over outright stock given macro uncertainty ahead of Sep 16.
ideas.catalyst: Azure 45% growth guide for Q1 FY27 (BofA note Sep 1, 2026); FOMC Sep 16 as pre-catalyst macro setup; earnings confirmed Oct 28, 2026
ideas.edge: Trading at ~$512 vs. consensus target $571 (+11.8% upside) and BofA target $600 (+17.2%); 55 analysts rate Strong Buy, zero Sell; Azure at $100B annualized with re-acceleration; tech sector expected to contribute 35.6% of S&P 500 earnings over next four quarters
ideas.bull_case: Azure re-acceleration to 45% confirms MSFT's AI monetization is ahead of schedule; a Sep 16 rate hold removes macro headwinds and sets up a multiple expansion into the Oct 28 print.
ideas.bear_case: Valuation is not cheap; a surprise Sep 16 rate hike could compress growth multiples and reset the swing entry lower; Azure growth already partially priced into current levels.

ideas.name: Invesco QQQ Trust
ideas.thesis: QQQ appeared in 3 of 6 overnight screens as the preferred macro expression vehicle for the NFP/FOMC binary sequence. With VIX at 14.32 (fell 5.8% Thursday) and FOMC hike/hold odds near 50/50, options premium is historically cheap ahead of two known volatility events within 12 days. Runs converged on a strangle or straddle structure to capture movement in either direction — a strong NFP reprices hike odds higher (QQQ negative), while a weak print is 'bad news is good news' (QQQ positive).
ideas.catalyst: August NFP release TODAY Sep 4 at 8:30 AM ET; FOMC rate decision Sep 16, 2026 at 2:00 PM ET
ideas.edge: VIX at 14.32 = relatively cheap options into two known binary catalysts within 12 days; ~50/50 hike vs. hold market pricing implies significant mispricing risk in either direction; Nasdaq up 1.4% Thursday with tech sector leading
ideas.bull_case: A benign NFP print today followed by a Sep 16 rate hold would extend Thursday's rally through month-end; QQQ's tech-heavy composition benefits directly from a lower-rate-for-longer narrative.
ideas.bear_case: A strong NFP could push hike odds toward 65%+ and trigger a sharp sell-off in rate-sensitive QQQ growth names; a hike on Sep 16 would be a material headwind for the index.
